subject: Genetics
title: Mutagens
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Mutagens.

hook.text: UV light hits your skin. It fuses two DNA letters together, creating a dimer. If unrepaired, that's a mutation.

buildup.text: Mutagens are agents that increase mutation rates: radiation, chemicals, and even some viruses damage DNA directly.

discovery.text: Tobacco smoke contains over 70 known mutagens. Each cigarette rolls the dice on thousands of DNA bases.

twist.text: Your body has DNA repair enzymes that fix thousands of lesions daily. Mutagens overwhelm the repair crew.

climax.text: Cancer isn't one mutation—it's an accumulation. Mutagens speed the clock. Time and exposure are the real killers.

punchline.text: Your DNA breaks every day. Repair keeps you alive.

quiz.question: How many known mutagens does tobacco smoke contain?
